section_2_pack_e_restoration_metrics.title: Agent C Boundary Review — Pack E Remember Restoration
section_2_pack_e_restoration_metrics.methodology: Per-item manual domain classification of all 4 choices against CMA Part 1 blueprint domains (A-F). ALIGNMENT_MAINTENANCE_GUIDE.md §2.1 decision tree (Q1→Q2→Q3). Agent B's automated domain classifier independently cross-checked and found unreliable (~85% error rate).

A.reason: ASC 820 fair value hierarchy (3 levels). Pure count recall — all numeric distractors.

B.reason: Cross-domain distractors enable domain-disjoint elimination per Q3 rule (>=2 cross-domain distractors).

E.reason: COSO IC 5 components (pure count), COSO Principle 7 (cross-domain distractors), COSO ERM 8 components (pure count).

confirmed_restorations.agent_b_classifier_accuracy: ~14.3% (10 of 70 correct). Agent B's 7-signal domain classifier systematically misclassified all-distractors-as-cross-domain — ~85.7% false-positive rate on Remember candidates.
confirmed_restorations.note: Of 70 candidates flagged by automated classifier, only 7 (10%) confirmed as genuine Remember. The remaining 63 (90%) have same-domain distractors requiring conceptual comprehension → correctly labeled Understand/Apply.

rejected_restorations.reason: All distractors are from the same CMA domain as the correct answer. Candidate must understand concept relationships, not just eliminate by domain. Agent B's classifier incorrectly labeled same-domain distractors as cross-domain.

escalated_item.escalation_reason: Q3 (3/3 cross-domain → Remember) conflicts with functional-purpose stem requiring conceptual comprehension. Decision tree conflict — human review needed.

section_8_biggest_surprise_finding.detail: 48 of 66 items (72.7%) labeled 'Analyze' are definition-match clones — stems describe a concept, answer is the TERM. These test Remember/Understand comprehension, not analysis. Only ~18 items are potentially genuine Analyze. Of the 1,161 Apply-labeled items, at least 4 are genuine Analyze (mislabeled). Section A — the domain richest in judgment scenarios — has ZERO Analyze items. The structural gap (need ~580 new items) means the pool cannot meet the 25% CAQS Analyze target without new content creation.
section_8_biggest_surprise_finding.second_finding: S719 UNDERSTAND OVERCORRECTION: 46.2% of pool is Understand (vs 15% CAQS target). 93% of pool is Understand+Apply. Cognitive spread is dangerously narrow — no room for genuine higher-order thinking items.
section_8_biggest_surprise_finding.third_finding: S719 ANALYTICS CONTAIN PHANTOM DATA: The official S719 Analytics Package and Distribution Analytics report pool-wide totals that include 12 B/C/D items never actually modified on disk. All downstream reports using S719 analytics as source data will carry this 12-item error.
section_8_biggest_surprise_finding.fourth_finding: PACK E USES A DIFFERENT TAXONOMY: Even after S719 normalization, Pack E diverges from Packs A-D on all 4 consistency patterns. Section E (Internal Controls) has 4 different dominant CLs across packs for equivalent content.
section_8_biggest_surprise_finding.fifth_finding: APPLY→UNDERSTAND IS THE BOUNDARY OF MAXIMUM CONFUSION: 86.3% of all reliability disagreements (88/102) occur at the Apply/Understand boundary. The classification system cannot reliably distinguish 'applying a procedure' from 'understanding how to apply a procedure.' This is the single biggest source of inter-rater disagreement.
